If the rejection is carried onto the PWU's own assurance axis, satisfaction is blocked PERMANENTLY: PWU.assuranceState REJECTED has ZERO out-arrows (derived from getMachine, not read), so REJECTED->SATISFIED is not on the matrix and the only in-arrow to workLifecycle SATISFIED requires assuranceState === 'SATISFIED'. So in that arrangement the refusal genuinely keys on a rejected mandatory assessment.

WHAT DEFEATS IT: NOTHING PERFORMS THE ROLLUP. `completeAssuranceAssessment` returning REJECTED writes the ASSESSMENT aggregate and does not touch the PWU's axes — measured, not read: after the REJECTED completion the PWU walked UNASSESSED -> EVIDENCE_REQUIRED -> READY_FOR_ASSESSMENT -> ASSESSING -> SATISFIED unimpeded, with the rejected assessment still reading REJECTED at the end. The quantifier 'ANY rejected mandatory assessment' is the whole rule and the engine has no reader for the set: the controller supplies `supportingObjectIds`, `rejectUnbackedDisposition` validates THOSE with `cited.some(...)`, and an assessment sitting REJECTED against a policy the PWU's own `assurancePolicyIds` names is never loaded. So the rule holds only when the professional volunteers the very fact the rule exists to force.

evidence:
WHAT THE LIMB FORBIDS: a mandatory parent obligation whose fate is not one of FOUR named classes — allocated to children, retained by parent, already satisfied, explicitly waived/superseded by valid authority. It is an EQUATION, so it is only 'the thing being checked' if all four terms are expressible and counted.

WHAT THE CODE DOES. `validateObligationConservation` (packages/rph-domain/src/decomposition.ts:62-84) unions exactly four sets — `allocated ∪ retained ∪ satisfied ∪ waived` (:65-68, :76-79) — over parent obligations whose `strength === 'MANDATORY'` (:74), and emits MISSING_OBLIGATION_ALLOCATION for any with none (:82). `buildObligationInput` (packages/rph-application/src/handlers/decomposition.ts:146-172) is the ONLY production site that fills those four sets. TERM BY TERM, AS THAT BUILDER SUPPLIES THEM:

  TERM 1, 'allocated to children' — DIVERGENT, DRIVEN, UNFILED. decomposition.ts:168 reads `allocatedObligationIds: [...allocations.map((a) => a.obligationId), ...objAllocated]`. It maps the allocation record to its `obligationId` and DISCARDS `allocatedTo`. `ObligationAllocationSchema` is `{ obligationId, allocatedTo: string[] }` (packages/rph-contracts/src/objects.ts:306-309), so the field naming the children EXISTS on the wire and no predicate at this site reads it. DRIVEN: a decomposition whose only disposition of a MANDATORY obligation is `{obligationId: OBL, allocatedTo: []}` — allocated to NOBODY — was marked VALID; and one allocating to a PWU that is not among `childWorkUnitIds` was also marked VALID. The engine's OWN oracle takes the opposite reading over the same field: packages/rph-engine/src/graph-conformance.ts:105-107 counts an obligation unallocated when `!targets || targets.length === 0 || !targets.every((t) => children.has(t))`, with the comment 'Allocated to NOTHING, or to something that is not a child of this decomposition, is not allocation.' Two committed sites, one field, opposite answers — and the command gate uses the weaker one.

  TERM 2, 'retained by parent' — LIVE AND CHECKED. decomposition.ts:169 reads the contract's `retainedParentObligationIds`. CONTROL 1 (identical decomposition, obligation retained) was ACCEPTED and the contract reached VALID, which is what proves the refusal in PROBE 1 discriminates rather than fires for everything.

  TERM 3, 'already satisfied' — UNREACHABLE. decomposition.ts:170 sources it ONLY from `satisfiedObligationIds: objSatisfied`, and `objSatisfied` is filled at :162 by `else if (status === 'SATISFIED')` on the OBLIGATION object. `Obligation.status` can never hold that value: the only OBLIGATION command mints at PROPOSED (packages/rph-application/src/handlers/obligation-constraint.ts:34, births declared at :39) and no handler advances the machine. DRIVEN: after five dispatch attempts the obligation still read PROPOSED.

  TERM 4, 'explicitly waived/superseded by valid authority' — UNREACHABLE, AND 'valid authority' IS NEVER CONSULTED EVEN IF IT WERE. `authorizedWaiverObligationIds: objWaived` (:171) is filled at :163 by `else if (status === 'WAIVED')`; the 'superseded' half is the `continue` at :159 on `status === 'SUPERSEDED'`. Both statuses are unreachable by the same census. No Decision, waiver object or authority reference is loaded on this path (contrast `buildConstraintInput`'s `authorityBasis` at :250-256, which DOES resolve a DECISION — the obligation half has no counterpart).

SO THE EQUATION THE ENGINE CHECKS IS A TWO-TERM ONE: `allocated(a record mentioning the id, holder unread) ∪ retained`. Two of canon's four classes cannot be put on the wire at all, and the first class is credited without its 'to children' qualifier.

The mechanism is at the cited site: collectConstraintFindings (rph-domain/src/decomposition.ts:186) groups records into a LIST per constraintId, folds their children into a `covered` SET (so N records naming one child collapse to a single 'covered' mark), then runs the per-record well-formedness loop at :208. Neither structure can see MULTIPLICITY: nothing anywhere counts dispositions per (constraint, child) pair. A second, weaker arrangement is also admitted (S13): PROPAGATED[A,B] + INAPPLICABLE[A,B] was refused only because the INAPPLICABLE record lacked an authority — i.e. the refusal was about that record's well-formedness, never about the contradiction. (b) 'retaining ... STRENGTH' — inexpressible: `propagatedStrength` (and a bare `strength`) on a propagation record is refused by ConstraintPropagationSchema's z.strictObject before any handler runs. So a propagation cannot declare it keeps MANDATORY, and the kernel arm that would check it (decomposition.ts:221, CONSTRAINT_WEAKENED_WITHOUT_AUTHORITY) is a dead predicate. (c) 'retaining AUTHORITY' — the propagation record carries no authority field, and more sharply the propagation never reaches the child at all: after ValidateDecomposition marked the contract VALID on a clean PROPAGATED[A,B], CHILD_A.constraintIds and CHILD_B.constraintIds were both [] and the CONSTRAINT object was still sitting on the parent at MANDATORY/PROPOSED. `state.constraintPropagations` is read at exactly ONE site in production — the validation gate itself (handlers/decomposition.ts:250) — so 'propagated' is a bookkeeping claim on the contract with no downstream carrier of authority or strength.
